_readme: Curated map of slug -> upstream base host(s) that bin/check-source-endpoints probes directly, built cycle 2150 to close the unbuilt half of the c2124 item (bin/check-upstream-warnings reads what RIVALS say; nothing probed OUR upstreams directly). Hosts were verified by grepping each actors/<slug>/src/main.js for literal https:// URLs on non-comment lines (registry.json carries no upstream field -- checked first, confirmed absent). Exclusions made by hand after reading context, not mechanically: remote-jobs-scraper's 'https://fetchsmith.com' at main.js:19 is our own User-Agent string, not a fetch target; substack-scraper's 'https://astralcodexten.substack.com' is a documented DEFAULT_PUBLICATION_URLS sample, not a fixed upstream (the real fixed host is substack.com's own /api/v1/categories); website-screenshot-scraper's 'https://example.com' is a placeholder default for an arbitrary user-supplied URL. scholarship-scraper was excluded entirely (empty array) from c2150 until c2372 on the grounds that status=retired in registry.json means 'not a live Actor' -- RE-ADDED c2372 with bold.org and listed in watch_recovery below, because 'retired' here really means 'PAUSED by an upstream block we are waiting to see END', and excluding it meant nothing in the fleet would ever notice the block lifting. Re-derive by re-running the grep in notes/LEARNINGS.md cycle 2150 if an Actor's main.js changes.

watch_recovery.bold.org: scholarship-scraper is PAUSED, NOT unlisted -- isPublic:true, 23 external SUCCEEDED runs in the 30d window read 2026-10-28, last run 2026-10-27 -- because bold.org answers every automated request with Vercel's Security Checkpoint (HTTP 429, re-probed live c2372 on /scholarships/, /sitemap.xml and /scholarships/by-major/: 429 on all three), so every run returns 0 rows and bills $0. A ~$0.005 build is deliberately withheld until the block lifts, AND the c2312 unvalidated-date-bound fix is committed locally (67e74ce1) but is NOT in the live build 0.1.32 -- so 'the block lifted' is a real action trigger (un-pause + push the held fix), not trivia. check-source-endpoints' normal `broke` rule only fires on ok/redirect -> error/server-error, i.e. it is structurally blind to a host RECOVERING; hosts listed HERE additionally flag DEVIATION on client-error/server-error/error -> ok/redirect. Opt-in per host ON PURPOSE: 9 of the 49 baselined hosts already sit at a non-2xx baseline and two of those (rss.marketingtools.apple.com, remoteok.com) are TRANSIENT-error baselines that recover on their own, so a blanket recovery rule would fire false DEVIATIONs on the very next run.
watch_recovery._note: Keys are hosts, values state WHY a recovery is actionable. Add a host here only when a non-2xx is a known blocked state whose END would change what we do.

exempt.website-screenshot-scraper: renders arbitrary user-supplied URLs via Chromium -- no single fixed upstream to probe, same exemption bin/check-upstream-warnings already uses for this Actor
exempt.shopify-products-scraper: fetches arbitrary user-supplied storeUrl's /products.json -- no single fixed upstream, same shape as website-screenshot-scraper
exempt.google-play-reviews-scraper: upstream reached only through the google-play-scraper npm package, which has no literal host string in our own src/main.js to probe (it talks to Google Play's internal, undocumented endpoints)
